open_points.subject: startup credential-header collision check
open_points.text: `capability:bindings.check_installed_instances`: no credential header has, case-insensitively, the name of a required header of its instance or of a header the kernel sets itself, `host` included (A09 rule 1). ... It reads only the installation — `capability:installation.selected_instance_name` and `capability:installation.manifest_source` — and the manifest, never the store.
open_points.question: How does `bindings.check_installed_instances` obtain each configured credential header name when neither named installation capability supplies it and no other public installation capability exposes it?
options: Add an installation capability that returns credential-header metadata without resolving the secret value
Have `load_installation` return credential-header metadata that `surface` passes to `bindings.check_installed_instances`
Make `bindings.check_installed_instances` call `resolve_service_credential`, despite credentials being resolved only when a service request is built
open_points.default_guess: Have `load_installation` return the non-secret credential-header metadata and pass it to `bindings.check_installed_instances`.

open_points.subject: pre-send instance failure classification
open_points.text: `base_url`: ... each is absent when the installation selects no instance or that instance does not state it ... At send `service_invoker` judges only the instance facts the ManifestOperation carries, and reads nothing from `installation` but the credential. ... (`instance_not_selected`, `instance_address_missing` — the same "counts as none" as A08 rule 5 —)
open_points.question: How can `service_invoker` distinguish `instance_not_selected` from `instance_address_missing` when `ManifestOperation` represents both situations with absent instance facts and the invoker may not read the selected-instance configuration?
options: Carry whether an instance was selected in `ManifestOperation`
Pass the selected-instance fact separately to `prepare_request`
Have `bindings.check_binding_current` return the appropriate pre-send failure instead of leaving both to `service_invoker`
Use one failure code for both situations
open_points.default_guess: Carry an explicit selected-instance-present fact with the instance facts returned to `service_invoker`.

open_points.subject: checks performed by check_installed_instances
open_points.text: for one it also selects an instance for, a manifest record that cannot be read or fails a check of the record itself (A08 rule 5) stops the start naming it
open_points.question: Which exact A08 rule 5 checks are applied at startup when no operation or proposed ports are named, given that rule 5 also contains operation-presence, effect-class, route, idempotency-key, proposal-port and request-shape checks?
options: Apply only service-record checks needed to locate the selected instance and its required headers
Validate every capability entry in the service record
Apply the checks to only operations referenced by accepted bindings
Remove the A08 rule 5 reference and state a separate ordered startup check list
open_points.default_guess: Apply a separately stated ordered subset covering the service record, selected instance and required-header facts needed for the collision check.
